settings.copy: Kiln & Coil is a working pottery studio where beginners and practiced hands share the same wheel. Throw, hand-build, glaze, and fire in a warm, unhurried space — with a kiln that's always warm and a teacher who never rushes you.

settings.title: How a piece
settings.intro: Every pot you see on our shelves took the same patient journey. Here's the path from a lump of clay to a piece you can hold, drink from, and keep.

steps.title: Throw or hand-build
steps.text: You start at the wheel or at the slab table — centering the clay, opening it, and pulling the walls up. Beginners get a steady hand on theirs until the first cylinder stands.

steps.title: Trim & refine
steps.text: Once the piece firms up, we trim the foot, smooth the seams, and add handles or texture. This is where a pot starts to feel like yours.

steps.title: Bisque fire
steps.text: The first firing hardens the clay into bisque — strong enough to glaze. We load the kiln together and wait for the temperature to tell us it's ready.

steps.title: Glaze & fire again
steps.text: You choose from our glaze wall, dip or brush your piece, and it goes back into the kiln for its final firing. A week later, it's yours to take home.

settings.note: Kiln & Coil is built on patience: if a piece cracks or slumps, we don't call it a failure — we call it a lesson, and we fire it again until you're proud of what you made.

settings.title: A studio that
settings.intro: Whether you've never touched clay or you're returning after years away, the studio is set up to let you work at your own pace — with real guidance, never hovering.

features.title: Small, unhurried classes
features.text: Six wheels, six students, one teacher. You get the attention you need without feeling watched — and the room stays calm enough to actually focus.

features.title: Everything included
features.text: Clay, glazes, tools, and both firings are part of every session. You never pay extra to see your work finished — it's all in the price.

features.title: A kiln that fires weekly
features.text: Our kilns run every week, so your pieces come home on a schedule you can count on — not whenever a batch happens to fill.

features.title: For every level
features.text: From a first-ever pinch pot to advanced glaze chemistry, the studio has a place for you. Returning students get open-studio time and their own shelf.

features.title: A teacher who stays
features.text: Our instructor has taught in this same room for twelve years. They know exactly when to step in and when to let a wobble become a lesson.

features.title: Work you can keep
features.text: Every piece you make is yours — food-safe, dishwasher-safe, and fired to last. Your shelf at home grows with every class.

settings.title: The feeling of
settings.intro: People come for a class and stay for a season. Here's a little of what they tell us as they carry their work home.

reviews.quote: I came in convinced I had no hand for it. Three months later I've got a shelf of mugs I actually use every morning. The teacher never once made me feel like I was behind.
reviews.author: Priya Raman

reviews.quote: The small classes are the whole difference. Six of us, one patient teacher, and a kiln that fires on schedule. My pieces actually come home — that's rarer than you'd think.
reviews.author: Marcus Bell

reviews.quote: I'd thrown in college and wanted to come back to it. This studio gave me open time, my own shelf, and zero pressure. It's the calmest two hours of my week.
reviews.author: Elena Ortiz
